newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, NATO differ on future relations after talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia, NATO differ on future relations after talks.

text.p: Russia and NATO on Tuesday failed to iron out differences holding up a deal on future relations between Moscow and the Western alliance, the Foreign Ministry said.

"A practical conversation took place. It was stated that positions on some issues became closer," it said in a brief statement after almost three hours of tense talks between Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.
"At the same time some difficult questions remain which must be resolved to pave the way for a mutually acceptable document on relations between Russia and NATO," the statement said.

Russia and NATO are working on a document which would define their relations after the Western alliance grants membership to some Eastern and Central European countries. First invitations are expected to be issued at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.
Russia bitterly opposes NATO expansion but has said it is ready to strike a deal which would ensure at least some of its security interests.
Moscow wants NATO to promise not to move its military infrastructure closer to Russian borders. It also wants a say in aspects of NATO activities which it says concern its security.
NATO says it is ready to meet some of Russia's security concerns in a loose charter. But it appears reluctant to accept any conditions which would affect rights of the new members.
